For Allow, 'the firewall denies traffic of the specified protocol type that does not match the domain specifications' (default action order); '.example.com matches example.com and matches all subdomains'; HTTPS is matched on the TLS SNI and HTTP on the Host header, not IP addresses; for traffic from other VPCs through a transit gateway, HOME_NET must include their CIDR ranges.

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Halsey Retail. All outbound traffic from the workload VPCs passes through AWS Network Firewall in a central inspection VPC, with a domain allow list: anything not listed is dropped. Tonight checkout switches to a new payment provider whose API is api.paynorth.example. Since the 21:00 switch every payment call times out. The old provider's contract ends at 23:00, when its API stops accepting requests.
handover: The firewall policy uses default action order; the allow list rule group is egress-allow (TLS_SNI and HTTP_HOST).
The change request for the new provider listed only the provider's website, www.paynorth.example.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the checkout services, the inspection VPC's firewall and its domain allow list, and the payment provider.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why payment calls failed, what you changed, and how vendor changes avoid it.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The egress firewall's domain allow list drops TLS whose SNI it does not name; the change added www.paynorth.example, which matches only itself, so api.paynorth.example was dropped.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Added api.paynorth.example and hooks.paynorth.example as explicit names; test payments passed. A pass-all rule opens every workload's egress; security group changes cannot affect an SNI drop.

parts.label: Vendor changes
parts.modelAnswer: Change requests must list the vendor's hostnames, and drops toward payment domains alarm.

scoring.modelReasoning: Timeouts to one new provider behind a domain allow list point at the list. The alert log shows drops on SNI api.paynorth.example, and the list names only www.paynorth.example, which matches only itself. Add the provider's two API hostnames as explicit names and verify a payment. A pass-all 443 rule removes the control for everyone; security groups cannot override a firewall SNI drop. Then require vendor hostnames in change requests and alarm on drops.
